title: Chapter 41: Demon
content:
Chapter 41:

Demon

His throat trembled as a war cry echoed through the dark, dense forest.

It wasn’t quite an “ah” or an “oh,” just an explosion of meaningless, nonsensical sound.

Even though it came from his own throat, Subaru himself couldn’t find any reason or meaning behind the act.

The red points of light lunged all at once.

As they drew closer, their outlines gradually took shape, revealing ferocious beasts clad in pitch black, baring their fangs as they attacked.

There was no time to register the trembling of his legs, the terror in his heart, or the scream of his soul.

The only thing dominating Subaru’s mind right then wasn’t the emotion toward the overwhelming embodiment of Death closing in on him, but the safety of the young girl lying right behind him.

He widened his stance, stretched out both arms, and used his body as a shield so the ferocious beasts’ claws and fangs wouldn’t reach behind him. It wasn’t a conscious choice. It was just a reaction; his body moved entirely on its own.

If these were opponents who would simply back down out of respect for his spirit, maybe he could have been saved. However, the reality closing in on him was merciless, and in the face of wild beasts driven by feral hunger, such sentimentality held absolutely no meaning.

—It’s over. Even though I finally saw the whole picture after coming all this way.

He lacked strength again. He couldn’t reach it again.

No matter how hard his heart refused to yield and struggled, pure lack of power snatched away Subaru’s options. Was this situation destined to be just the same?

“————————!!”

He roared, refusing to accept surrender.

He maintained his fighting spirit to the bitter end, determined not to lose to any of the points of light before him in that regard alone. It was literally a hollow, papier-mâché bluff—fangs bit into his windpipe and,

—Right before his eyes, he saw the witchbeast’s head burst like a piece of fruit.

Blood splattered from the point-blank bludgeoning, showering Subaru, who was directly in front, in fresh blood from head to toe. Immediately after, the headless body crashed into Subaru, carrying all of its original momentum. Blown backward and sent tumbling, Subaru shook his head and stood up, reeling from the pain and the unpleasant sensation of blood.

Just what on earth

—he thought, when,

“Rem is late, but—she is glad she made it in time.”

With a graceful flutter of her skirt hem, lightly pinching her white apron dress with one hand while gripping a vicious iron ball in the other, the blue-haired girl descended into the abyss.

She spun around, taking a gentle step, the sound of her chain echoing.

“Rem believes we agreed you would focus entirely on buying time?”

“I tried my best! I bought so much time! I even went at it with a ‘it’s totally fine if I just defeat it’ kinda vibe! And here’s the result, seriously thank you so very much!”

Subaru literally threw himself onto the ground in prostration, offering his thanks to Rem, who was making a series of high-pitched clinks with the chain of her morning star.

Glancing sideways at his reaction, Rem slowly looked forward—at the pack of witchbeasts, licking their chops and sizing them up with the arrival of new prey.

The creatures that had been so belligerent toward Subaru alone instantly switched to a cautious stance with the addition of just one petite girl. They absolutely did not take lightly the fact that one of their pack had been slaughtered in an instant.

He already knew this from his exchange with the single one earlier, but despite their beastly appearance, these things were incredibly shrewd and cunning.

“Rem…”

He called out to her back as she stood firmly, urging her to be on guard.

Rem didn’t look back at Subaru’s deliberately lowered voice, simply letting out a sigh.

“Rem followed your terrible body odor, rushed over upon hearing those unashamedly bizarre screams, and this is what she finds. You are hardly in a decent state.”

“Being told I have terrible body odor hurts a little. Also, I don’t remember doing that, so I’d love to hear exactly what I was screaming later.”

“If Rem feels like it. And if 

they

 allow it, she wouldn’t mind telling you in excruciating detail.”

Pointing the iron handle straight ahead, Rem harbored a dangerous light in her eyes, almost as if provoking them. While it sent chills down Subaru’s spine, the witchbeasts on the receiving end of that hostility clearly weren’t feeling calm about it either. A clear readiness to engage and an eagerness to trample surfaced in the eyes of the creatures glaring silently at them.

“It seems that will be impossible.”

“—Rem!”

Unable to hold it in, Subaru instinctively screamed Rem’s name.

What suddenly occurred right in front of her was a fierce attack by two witchbeasts splitting to the left and right. Just as they closed the distance to her to within a few steps, the two running side-by-side simultaneously broke off in opposite directions.

Had it been Subaru facing them, his mind wouldn’t have been able to keep up with which one to focus on, and he would have been effortlessly torn apart by their venomous fangs.

However,

“————Hah!”

Her right arm, gripping the iron handle, swung out carelessly, as if swatting a bug. The swing brought the chain attached to the handle with it, and the iron ball connected to the chain followed suit.

The supposedly sluggish, heavy weapon of destruction spun with terrifying speed, sweeping away everything in its trajectory following the swing of her arm. It scored a direct hit on the torso of a witchbeast caught in its path, blowing it away with enough force to snap its body clean in half. Bones and internal organs scattered, instantly turning into unnoticed fertilizer for the forest.

Then, the remaining one, its partner killed in an instant, poured all its rage into its fangs, delivering a sharp strike to Rem’s wide-open left side—just before it landed, her left fist shot straight down onto the witchbeast’s snout. The sheer power of the punch caved its skull in, killing it instantly with a blow that buried its head into the ground.

It was a brilliant display of skill. But the gruesomeness of it was far removed from words like ‘brilliant.’

Words of praise escaped him; Subaru could only stare wide-eyed at the massacre taking place right in front of him, utterly dumbfounded.

He thought he had experienced Rem’s destructive power firsthand. It became blatantly clear, both in name and reality, that it had indeed been nothing more than a ‘thought.’

“S-So stroooooooooong!!”

“Rem wonders if that is an appropriate word to use for a lady, Subaru.”

“For a guy with a vocabulary as poor as mine, this is the only word that comes to mind to describe the current situation. Seriously, you’re unbelievable.”

Seeing a level of reliability in Rem that far exceeded his imagination, Subaru vaulted up and returned to his original spot.

Crawling back, Subaru checked on the fallen girl. In this desperate situation, with her life in ongoing, immediate danger, the sleeping girl remained completely oblivious, continuing to sleep soundly.

“Wow, talk about carefree and easygoing. She’s definitely gonna grow up to be energetic and full of 

grit!”

1

Praising her masterful sleeping form, he used his aching arm to scoop up her small body. He readjusted his hold so as not to drop the light weight.

“Rem, any chance you could wipe them all out by yourself?!”

“We are heavily outnumbered. It would be a war of attrition.”

“Yeah, figures. Very well then…”

Still carrying the girl, he moved to Rem’s side.

Having lost two more of their pack, the witchbeasts were sluggish. They lowered their bodies, seeming to gauge their next move. Though their glares were intimidating, they lacked the opening to take action. If they had simply relied on their numbers and launched a wave attack, Subaru and Rem, with their inferior combat power, wouldn’t have stood a chance.

However, they mistook caution for cowardice and threw away their best option of their own accord.

Therefore, Subaru and Rem simultaneously locked eyes on the exact same spot, and,

“There!”

Rem’s strike answered Subaru’s shout.

The roar of the iron ball pierced the air, cheering on the slaughter. It flew true, exploding against the ground right in front of the spot where the witchbeast pack was densest—clods of earth and dust flew into the air, and a waterfall of dirt and rocks blinded the leaping witchbeasts for several seconds.

“Now—!”

At Rem’s next shout, Subaru’s body shot forward as if he’d been kicked.

He aimed straight for a breakthrough point in the dense formation, a gap forced open by that single strike—.

The witchbeasts that had yielded the path roared at Subaru as he dove into the gap. Barking, the fierce beasts leaped again to block Subaru’s path, but,

“—Uwoooh, the trauma sound!!”

The light, clear sound of a chain gently brushed past his ear as he ran.

A shudder raced up Subaru’s spine at that refrain from the other time. Right beside him, the iron ball’s welcoming blast exploded, and a flower of blood bloomed magnificently in the night forest.

Leaving the fresh blood behind, he trampled over the uncertain footing, plunging into the forest while being exposed to immense hostility. Leaping over tree roots, his cheeks slapped by branches,

“Rem, I don’t know the way!”

“Straight ahead! Once we pass through the barrier, we win. Do not lose your sense of direction until then!”

Even told to go straight, ‘straight ahead’ was uncertain.

He hadn’t expected the darkness, where he could only see slightly ahead, to throw off his sense of direction this much. Even if he wanted to grope his way forward, both hands were occupied by the weight of the girl.

Naturally, while watching out for obstacles ahead, Subaru was forced to hunch his body over, running while trying to minimize any harm to the girl.

He was out of breath. Had he lost the path? Would they catch up? Were they waiting ahead, were they surrounded?

His anxieties were endless, and the welling terror was steadily chipping away at Subaru’s mind.

The sensation in his left arm was dull; the bleeding wouldn’t stop, dripping from the fabric of his jacket. He even had the illusion that the drops of blood falling to the ground were leaving a trail for their pursuers.

He ran, he dashed, he kept fleeing.

The same scenery continued, making him feel as though he wasn’t advancing a single step. He knew that couldn’t be true, but his impatience spurred on the imagination.

And every time his complaints swelled in his chest and his knees felt like giving out,

—The sound of the undulating chain from behind spurred Subaru on.

Every time he heard that sound, Subaru gritted his back teeth and looked forward.

The only reason he was able to run like this right now was thanks to Rem. Because she was eliminating the external enemies and continuing to protect Subaru’s back, he was able to expose his shameful struggle to survive like this.

Since he’d already exposed this much anyway. He might as well throw away his reputation and show them how pathetically he could struggle to live.

“Ah, shit! My side hurts—!”

He spurred himself on with a shout born of displaced anger and forced his legs forward.

Forward, forward—!

Then, suddenly, the darkness opened up before Subaru’s eyes.

His field of vision widened. Squinting involuntarily at the sudden change, he saw artificial lights burning in the distance.

“Rem! Lights! People… We’re gonna reach the barrier!”

At the appearance of literal salvation, Subaru turned his head back to relay his joy.

However, immediately after, he found his eyes frozen wide open.

Because the sight of Rem, fighting behind him and protecting his back, was far too gruesome.

Across her stiffly starched, well-tailored maid uniform, numerous lacerations from either claws or fangs were carved. Countless deep wounds marred her exposed white skin, and her once vividly bright blue hair was in complete disarray, showered from the head down in so much blood spatter that its original color was indiscernible.

“Rem—!”

“Run…! While Rem is, while Rem is still Rem!”

Subaru’s voice, full of concern for her, was cut off by her forceful words from behind.

He couldn’t accept it. But, shaking off his hesitation at her scream, he ran toward the barrier.

Putting all sentimentality on hold, if he could just get past the barrier, if he could just get through there—

“What…?”

His resolve was instantly shattered by an unexpected sight right at the start.

Subaru’s dumbfounded gaze—it was directed right beside the massive tree where the crystal controlling the barrier was embedded. His gaze ran low, almost parallel to the ground. Crouching in that spot was a tiny, tiny little shadow.

As he got closer, as its outline became clearer, Subaru’s eyes widened.

It was a tiny creature. Its body was small enough to be completely enveloped in both arms, its fur as soft as fluff, a size that couldn’t even compare to the large ones.

—It was the puppy witchbeast that had guided Subaru to the village.

“I wondered why I hadn’t seen you… but hey, even I can kick your ass!”

If it intended to play ‘you shall not pass’, it was overwhelmingly lacking in weight.

If it planned on standing as the final obstacle in this desperate escape, he had to definitively state that its thinking was incredibly shallow.

That thought of Subaru’s,

“You’re kidding…”

Was washed away by the mudslide that unfolded before his eyes, completely covering his field of vision.

It was a sight that made him realize just exactly who had been guilty of shallow thinking.

His world slowly, gently ground to a halt. Subaru understood from personal experience that this was the grace period granted when one was on the brink of death.

In this world where everything moved at a glacial pace, there was something he realized far too late.

Before entering the forest, Rem had spoken to Subaru like so.

—That witchbeasts are the enemies of mankind that possess magical force.

She didn’t say they could use curses. She said they possessed magical force. Didn’t that mean they could also use magic like this?

“Ooooooooooooh—!!”

He thrust his legs out sideways, applying sudden brakes to his full-speed sprint. But it was meaningless. His pitching body lost its balance, and the mudslide was already right in front of him. There was no way to evade it. And if he was swallowed by the flow, the mad frenzy of sand and stone would tear his body to shreds in an instant.

All was lost.

The moment that thought ran through his mind, Subaru braced himself to at least throw the girl in his arms to the side—when an impact from directly beside sent him blasting away, hurtling through the trees.

“Ogoaah?!”

Struck around his right flank with a force that felt like it would spill his internal organs, he screamed as he flew through the air. In a gravity-defying sensation where up, down, left, and right all blurred together, he simply curled his body to protect the girl, crashing back-first into a thick trunk, losing his breath, and falling to the ground.

“Gah, ahf, aah… It hurts…!”

Groaning in pain, he looked up while clutching his struck abdomen.

And then, he witnessed Rem being launched up above the trees by a direct hit from the mudslide.

Receiving the violent welcome of earth and stone, Rem’s small body danced lightly like a fallen leaf. Spraying blood everywhere, her state was completely different from when she was simply covered in blood spatter earlier; even to an untrained eye, it was obvious she had taken critical damage.

Just like that, unable to catch herself, Rem’s body slammed violently into the ground. The only saving grace was that the earth, tilled by the mudslide, hadn’t crushed the falling girl’s head.

Now that things had come to this, even someone as slow to catch on as Subaru could grasp the situation.

Rem had sacrificed the time she needed to evade in order to shove Subaru, who was frozen in the face of the mudslide, out of the way. And as a result, she ended up taking the full brunt of the impact herself.

Of course, it was a force Subaru could never have withstood even if he had taken it. But if Rem ended up being sacrificed because of it, then it was all meaningless.

“Rem, you idiot! You, doing this… this makes my…!”

The moment he was about to scream ‘what was it all for,’ a chill ran down Subaru’s spine.

Most likely, they felt the exact same sensation. The witchbeast that unleashed the mudslide, and the pursuing pack that had caught up, all ceased their movements at once.

There was a premonition. There was certainty. Only the dense scent of Death drifted through the air.

—Slowly, Rem’s fallen body was rising.

Despite taking such a violent attack, there were no signs of injury in her movements as she stood up. On the contrary, the wounds she should have suffered were closing right before his eyes. Her tremendous healing power generated intense heat, evaporating the blood and even creating a red mist.

And he saw it. Subaru saw it.

Rem, turning to glare around her, her eyes devoid of reason.

Her face, smeared with blood spatter, twisted into a smile of ecstasy, and above all—her figure, with a white horn growing from her head where her hair ornament had come off.

“Aha, hahaha—”

Laughter. It was a laugh that spilled from a naked cruelty, much like a young girl’s.

Spinning around, Rem’s body rode the wind and charged into the pack. Before the lead witchbeast, which had stopped in its tracks, could even react, the back of its neck was crushed by Rem’s heel. She had the witchbeast's throat crushed from directly above to extinguish its life, then kicked its carcass with all her might to keep the other waiting witchbeasts in check. Starting with the ones that hesitated, she swung the morning star in her hand—the chain retracted into the iron handle, turning it into a mace—smashing them over and over again, mass-producing flowers of blood and corpses one after another.

“

Witchbeast

, 

witchbeast

, 

witchbeast

—

Witch

!!”

What was most terrifying was that Rem, despite her eyes having lost their reason, had not lost her sanity.

Even while surrendering herself to her surging bestiality, she hadn’t lost sight of the situation. With her overwhelming power, she was venting some smoldering grudge held deep within her.

Blood burst, skulls were crushed, intestines and brain matter were scattered across the forest with tremendous force.

On his knees, forgetting even his pain, Subaru was mesmerized by the sight.

Right now, he lacked the courage to raise his voice. He couldn’t shake the feeling that if he did, if he entered the awareness of the rampaging Rem, she might kill him—even though he knew she wouldn’t.

Or perhaps it wasn’t a misunderstanding. That was how completely unhinged Rem looked right now.

That figure, that grotesque form covered in blood spatter, echoing maniacal laughter through the forest, was truly,

“—A 

demon.”

2

No matter how much blood spatter she bathed in, only that white horn remained forever unsullied.

Atop her head, it gleamed with a sharp point, as if loudly proclaiming its existence.

Subaru was swallowed up by the situation.

However, unlike the paralyzed Subaru, the witchbeasts weren’t about to just sit there and wait to be slaughtered. The individuals that broke free from their rigidity surrounded Rem one after another, and even as the pile of corpses grew with every strike, they slowly began to reach her body with their claws and fangs.

They had been heavily outnumbered to begin with. The number of witchbeasts, which had only grown as they moved through the forest, was immeasurable. She should have already crushed a number equal to the initial pack, yet the red points of light floating in the dark night continued to swell without end.

“Even in ultimate invincible mode, against infinitely respawning enemies, there’s no way she can last forever…”

The situation was changing dizzyingly fast, but the underlying fact remained: Subaru and Rem were at a disadvantage.

Just as Subaru objectively understood this, he cut off his own words at the sign of magical force swelling once again.

Magical force was beginning to concentrate, and once again, it was around that puppy.

The magical force in the atmosphere was being gathered there by the roots, twisting his vision as if it were warping. Rem must have felt the vortex of magic. Turning around to deal with the threat, she readied a hand coated in the guts of the witchbeasts she had just eviscerated and aimed for the puppy—but,

—Not missing the opportunity of her trying to sprint forward, the pack of witchbeasts lunged for her back all at once.

“————!”

A hint of agitation. Even the rampaging Rem seemed dumbfounded by a situation that exceeded her own understanding.

Emotion returned to the eyes that had lost their reason; the bloodstained, maniacal smile suddenly crumbled, and beneath it, the face of a grief-stricken girl appeared.

—Ah, so she can make a face like that too

; a thought somewhere in the back of his mind.

“—Gaaaaaaaaaaaah!!!”

At the agonizing pain of his left arm being crushed, Subaru let out a scream that felt like it would tear his throat apart.

Immediately after, the sensation of fangs buried themselves simultaneously into his right leg, left flank, and back. His vision dyed completely red. The pain could no longer even be comprehended as pain. His ankle was shattered. A massive chunk of flesh was taken from his flank. Blood, his insides, were leaking out. Spilling out. What a waste. 

My flesh and blood.

“Subaru—!!”

He heard a voice that sounded like a scream.

He tried to look up toward the direction he heard it, but his body wouldn’t obey him anymore. His balance was gone. The ankle opposite to the shattered one was also torn halfway off; the severity of the wounds was just about perfectly balanced now. He collapsed to the ground. Right in front of his eyes, a maw lined with fangs closed in. Fangs aiming for his windpipe. Right in front of him, it was crushed flat between the iron ball and the ground. Blood scattered. Was it his own blood, or something else.

His consciousness was fading. He didn’t know what would happen when it disappeared.

His life was spilling away. What an incredibly stupid thing he had done, even he thought so himself. Starting over but fixating too much on that completely defeated the purpose, putting the cart before the horse.

It hurts, it’s agonizing, it’s far, I can’t see, I can’t hear, my life is wearing away.

From the hole in his flank, his life was spilling out like sand from an hourglass.

I’m disappearing, it’s ending, everything—I.

“Don’t die, don’t die, don’t die—!”

A voice that sounded like it was about to cry.

A crying voice.

I—.
